argument: The verified source convex hull contains the h0 disk and consists of original source vertices. For any rotation and signed axis, a source vertex attains projection >=h0. Center flooring changes its projection/norm by less than sqrt(2), yielding projection>h0-2=h and norm<R0+2=R, hence transverse absolute coordinate<=L. A center in a strip outer axial band therefore places this actual source vertex strictly inside the source-contained rectangle: the near edge follows from support h, the far edge from width>R-core, and both transverse edges from strict L margins. In the central axial band, distance to the rectangle is <=core<inner, so the source-contained cog disk intersects its interior. The original source polygon near a vertex strictly inside the rectangle has positive-area overlap. This holds for both signs and axes. The convex hull is used only to certify a source vertex support, never as filled source collision geometry. The checked inequalities apply to every fixed and moving rectangle listed.
